mainTopic: The second rainfall and its laws, the curse of 'וְעָצַר', and the ברכה on rain
overview: This amud is all about rain. First the גמרא lists laws that depend on the רביעה שניה, the second rainfall of the season: a נדר 'until the rains,' the olives left for the poor, walking on שבילי הרשות, and removing שביעית straw and hay. Along the way it explains the word נמושות and brings a פסוק showing that שביעית produce must be removed once it is gone from the field. רבי אבהו then explains that רביעה means rain that makes the earth fertile, and he gives how much rain counts as the first and second rainfall. רב חסדא gives several rules about when the curse of 'וְעָצַר' is not in effect: enough rain to seal a barrel, rain before the evening שמע, and the right amount of rain in part of the country. Each rule is tested with a challenge and answered. The גמרא also discusses when rain in טבת is good for the year. Finally, רבי אבהו says when to make a ברכה on rain, and the גמרא gives its wording and corrects the closing words to 'אֵל הַהוֹדָאוֹת'. רב פפא begins a practical ruling that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A vow 'until the rains' lasts until the second rainfall
steps.stepSummary: A source rules that if someone makes a נדר lasting 'until the rains,' the vow covers the period from when the rains start until the רביעה שניה falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows that something is forbidden to him 'until the rains,' the vow lasts from when the rains start to fall until the second rainfall comes down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing one practical use of the 'second rainfall': it decides how long a נדר 'until the rains' lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until the rains' are vague, because rain can fall over several weeks. The ruling gives them a clear end point: the 'time of the rains' ends with the רביעה שניה. So the vow stays in force until that rainfall comes.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow (נדר) forbidding something to himself
The second rainfall of the rainy season

phrases.english: One who vows until the rains:
from when rains fall
until the second rainfall falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by showing one practical use of the second rainfall (vows).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow 'until the rains' lasts from the start of the rains until the רביעה שניה.

steps.title: רב זביד: the second rainfall matters for olives left for the poor
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the רביעה שניה also matters for olives. He brings a משנה that sets when anyone, not just the poor, may take לקט, שכחה, פאה, פרט, עוללות, and olives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: it matters for olives. As we learned in a משנה: From when may anyone take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and corner produce? From when the נמושות have left. Single grapes and small clusters? From when the poor have gone through the vineyard and come back. Olives? From when the second rainfall falls.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives another practical use of the second rainfall and backs it up with a משנה about gifts to the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some produce is set aside only for the poor. At some point the poor are clearly done, and then anyone may take what is left. For fields and vineyards, that point is when the last poor people have passed through. For olives, the משנה uses the רביעה שניה as the sign that the poor have finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Stalks that fall during harvest and are left for the poor
Sheaves forgotten in the field, left for the poor
The corner of the field left unharvested for the poor
Single grapes that fall during the grape harvest
Small, incompletely formed grape clusters left for the poor
A term for the last group of poor gleaners (explained in the next steps)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the second rainfall acts as a fixed public marker in agricultural law, not just a weather event.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: For olives.
phrases.notes: He means the second rainfall also matters for a law about olives.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: From when are all people
permitted to take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and corner produce?
From when the namoshot have left.
Single grapes and small clusters?
From when the poor have gone through the vineyard and come back.
Olives?
From when the second rainfall falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second practical use of the second rainfall, this time in the laws of gifts to the poor.
steps.raayaObject: That the רביעה שניה has legal significance for olives
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing when anyone may take gifts left for the poor
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may take the olives left for the poor once the second rainfall falls.

steps.title: What does the word 'נמושות' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask what נמושות, the word used in the משנה, means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'נמושות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside to ask about a hard word from the משנה it just quoted. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to רב זביד. It is a side question about a word. Knowing who the נמושות are tells us exactly when anyone may take לקט, שכחה, and פאה.

phrases.english: What are namoshot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question on a word from the משנה in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term נמושות

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: old men who walk with a cane
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that נמושות are old men who walk with a staff.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: old men who walk with a staff.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: the נמושות are elderly poor people who walk with a cane.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old men with canes move slowly and are usually the last to pass through the field. Once even they have gone, the poor are clearly finished, and anyone may take what is left.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Old men who walk with a staff.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סָבֵי דְּאָזְלִי אַתִּיגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נמושות are elderly men who walk with a cane.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the gleaners who come after the gleaners
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains נמושות as the last round of gleaners, who come after the earlier gleaners have finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: gleaners after gleaners.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different explanation of the word נמושות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the word does not describe old age. It describes order: the group that comes after the other gleaners. Once this last group has passed, anyone may take what is left.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleaners, people who collect leftover produce

steps.whatToRemember: Both explanations of נמושות point to the last poor people to go through the field. רבי יוחנן says they are slow old men, and ריש לקיש says they are the round of gleaners after the other gleaners.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Gleaners after gleaners.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לָקוֹטֵי בָּתַר לָקוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that רבי יוחנן answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נמושות are the gleaners who come after the other gleaners.

steps.title: רב פפא: the second rainfall ends permission to walk on field paths
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the רביעה שניה matters for שבילי הרשות. People may walk on the paths through private fields until the second rainfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it matters for walking on the permitted paths. As the Master said: Everyone may walk on the permitted paths until the second rainfall falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list of uses for the second rainfall, and רב פפא adds a third: the time limit for walking on paths through private fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People are normally allowed to walk on certain paths through someone else's field. After the second rainfall the fields are plowed and planted, so walking there would damage the crops. That is why the permission ends at the רביעה שניה.

keyTerms.meaning: Paths through private fields that people are allowed to use
As the Master said (introduces a known teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The רביעה שניה is a time marker in several areas of הלכה: it sets the end of a נדר 'until the rains,' it lets anyone take the olives left for the poor, and it ends the permission to walk on שבילי הרשות.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For walking on the permitted paths.
phrases.notes: These are paths through someone else's field that people are allowed to use.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Everyone may walk on the permitted paths
until the second rainfall falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּדֵי לְהַלֵּךְ בִּשְׁבִילֵי הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about נמושות and returns to listing uses of the second rainfall.
steps.raayaObject: That the רביעה שניה matters for walking on שבילי הרשות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People may walk on the permitted paths through fields only until the second rainfall.

steps.title: The second rainfall sets the deadline for removing שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the רביעה שניה matters for בעור of שביעית produce, and supports this with a משנה about straw and hay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the second rainfall matters for removing שביעית produce. As we learned in a משנה: Until when may one benefit from and burn the straw and hay of שביעית? Until the second rainfall falls.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds one more law that depends on the second rainfall. He backs it up by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins the list from רב זביד and רב פפא. The משנה says straw and hay of שביעית may be used only until the second rainfall. After that, they must be removed and may no longer be used.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove. Here it means getting rid of שביעית produce from one's home once its time is up.
Produce that grew during the seventh year (שמיטה), which has special holiness and rules
As we learned in a משנה
Straw and stubble or hay, the leftover stalks after a harvest

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
[The second rainfall matters] for removing the produce of the seventh year.
As we learned in a mishna:
Until when may one benefit from and burn
the straw and the hay of the seventh year?
Until the second rainfall falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לְבַעֵר פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית. דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the list of laws tied to the second rainfall, after רב פפא's paths
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second rainfall is the deadline for using and removing שביעית straw and hay

steps.title: Why must שביעית produce be removed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind the rule that שביעית produce must be removed at a set time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why there is a deadline at all for keeping שביעית produce. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but not the reason. The גמרא wants to know what makes the time run out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A standard question asking for the source or logic behind a rule

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule quoted in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for removing שביעית produce once it is gone from the field

steps.title: The פסוק: your animals may eat only while wild animals still can
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links feeding your animals at home to wild animals eating in the field. When the food is gone from the field, it must be removed from the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And for your cattle and for the wild animals that are in your land.' As long as the wild animal eats in the field, feed your cattle in the house. Once the food is gone for the wild animal from the field, remove it for your cattle from the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that ties your right to use שביעית produce at home to what is still available in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts your own animals and the wild animals side by side. So the rule is that your animals may eat only as long as the wild animals can. After the second rainfall the straw and hay in the fields are ruined, so the time to use them at home ends too.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written, used to bring a פסוק
Your cattle, meaning tame animals kept at home
A wild animal that finds its food in the field
It is used up or gone

steps.whatToRemember: The time for using שביעית produce at home ends when that type of produce is gone from the field. For straw and hay, that happens at the second rainfall.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And for your cattle and for the wild animals that are in your land,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:7

phrases.english: as long as the wild animal eats in the field,
feed your cattle in the house.
Once it is gone for the wild animal from the field,
remove it for your cattle from the house.
phrases.notes: It is a play on words: כָּלָה means 'it ran out,' and כַּלֵּה means 'finish it off' or 'remove it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 25:7 pairs your cattle with the wild animals, so use at home ends when the produce is gone from the field

steps.title: What the word רביעה means
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that rain is called רביעה because it makes the ground fertile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What does the word 'רביעה' mean? Something that makes the ground fertile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of rain. רבי אבהו explains why rainfall is called רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רביעה comes from רובע, a word used for an animal mating. Rain is pictured as making the earth 'give birth' to plants. The next step brings support for this picture.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording or term, here meaning the meaning of a word
Fertilizes, related to the word used for animals mating

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
What is the meaning of the word "revia" [rainfall]?
Something that fertilizes the ground.
phrases.notes: רובע is the word for an animal mating, so rain is pictured as making the earth 'pregnant' with plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of laws and turns to the meaning of the word רביעה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רביעה means rain that fertilizes the ground

steps.title: Rain is the husband of the earth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו's explanation matches רב יהודה, who calls rain the earth's husband and proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רב יהודה, for רב יהודה said: Rain is the husband of the earth, as it says: 'For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there unless they have watered the earth, and made it give birth and sprout.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אבהו's explanation fits a teaching of רב יהודה. רב יהודה backs it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says rain makes the earth 'give birth' (והולידה). That is the language of a husband and wife. This supports reading רביעה as fertilizing.

phrases.english: This is like Rav Yehuda, as Rav Yehuda said:
Rain is the husband of the earth,
as it is stated: "For as the rain comes down
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 55:10

phrases.english: and the snow from heaven,
and does not return there
unless it has watered the earth
and made it give birth and sprout."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's explanation with רב יהודה's teaching
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's explanation that רביעה means fertilizing

steps.title: How much rain counts as the first and second rainfall
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives amounts: the first rainfall must soak a טפח into the ground. The second must make enough mud to seal a barrel's opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: The first rainfall is enough rain to go a טפח into the ground. The second is enough to seal the opening of a barrel with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defines how much rain counts as each rainfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we knew the dates of the rainfalls, but not how much rain counts. Light rain does not count. The first rainfall must soak a טפח deep. The second must turn the ground into mud thick enough to plug a barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall of the season

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
The first rainfall
is enough to go a handbreadth into the ground.
The second
is enough to seal the opening of a barrel with it.
phrases.notes: He means the ground gets so muddy that you could use the mud to plug a barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי אבהו about rain, this time about amounts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First rainfall: soaks a טפח deep. Second rainfall: makes mud enough to seal a barrel.

steps.title: Enough rain to seal a barrel means no curse of ועצר
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that if rain fell enough to make mud for sealing a barrel, the year is not under the curse of 'ועצר את השמים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Rains that fell enough to seal the opening of a barrel with them do not count as 'and He will close up' the heavens.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא uses רבי אבהו's measure to tell us when the curse of ועצר is not in effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים warns that ה׳ will 'close up the heavens' if we sin. רב חסדא says that once this much rain has fallen, the curse was not fulfilled. He uses the same measure that רבי אבהו gave for the second rainfall in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And He will close up' the heavens, the curse of no rain

steps.whatToRemember: The second rainfall is measured by mud enough to seal a barrel. That same amount is enough to show the curse of ועצר did not happen.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Rains that fell
enough to seal the opening of a barrel with them
do not count as "and He will close up."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:17

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גְּשָׁמִים שֶׁיָּרְדוּ כְּדֵי לָגוּף בָּהֶן פִּי חָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the barrel-sealing measure from step 12 to define when the curse of ועצר is not in effect
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain enough to seal a barrel means the curse of ועצר was not fulfilled

steps.title: Rain before reading 'and He will close up' cancels the curse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that if rain fell before one recites the words 'וְעָצַר' in קריאת שמע, that rain shows the curse is not in effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Rain that falls before 'and He will close up' is read does not count as 'and He will close up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives another rule about rain. If rain fell before you reached the words 'וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם' in שמע, then that time is not under the curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 measured rain by amount: enough to make mud for sealing a barrel. Here רב חסדא measures by timing: rain that comes before the curse is recited shows the curse is not active right now.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And He will close up' (the heavens), the curse of no rain in the second paragraph of שמע
it does not count as / it is not in the category of

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Rain that fell before 'and He will close up,'
phrases.notes: He means before you say these words in the second paragraph of שמע (דברים 11:17).

phrases.english: does not count as 'and He will close up.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רב חסדא about when the curse of 'וְעָצַר' does not apply, this time based on timing instead of amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain that falls before one recites 'וְעָצַר' in שמע shows the curse is not in effect.

steps.title: אביי limits the rule to the evening שמע
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב חסדא's rule only works for rain before the evening שמע. Rain before the morning שמע can still count as the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this about rain before the evening 'and He will close up.' But rain before the morning 'and He will close up' can still count as the curse.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב חסדא's rule. Rain that fell during the day, before the evening שמע, is a good sign. Rain early in the morning, before the morning שמע, is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not reject רב חסדא's rule. He limits it to one case. The reason for this limit comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this about... (a phrase that limits an earlier rule)

phrases.english: Abaye said: We only said this
about rain before the 'and He will close up' of the evening,
but rain before the 'and He will close up' of the morning
does still count as 'and He will close up.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב חסדא's rule from step 14 to rain before the evening שמע only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only rain before the evening שמע cancels 'וְעָצַר'. Rain before the morning שמע may still be part of the curse.

steps.title: Morning clouds have no substance
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his limit with רב יהודה בר יצחק, who says morning clouds have no substance, and proves it from a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה בר יצחק said: Morning clouds have no substance, as it is written: 'What shall I do for you, אפרים? What shall I do for you, יהודה? Your kindness is like a morning cloud...'
steps.whatsHappening: This explains why morning rain does not count. Morning clouds are weak and pass quickly, so they do not bring real rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the people's weak, short-lived kindness to a morning cloud, which shows that morning clouds have no lasting value. So a little rain from morning clouds is not a sign that the curse has ended.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda bar Yitzchak said:
These morning clouds
have no substance in them,
as it is written: 'What shall I do for you, Ephraim,'
what shall I do for you, Judah,
your kindness is like a morning cloud, etc.'
phrases.notes: הושע 6:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and proof behind אביי's limit in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that rain before the morning שמע does not cancel 'וְעָצַר'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה בר יצחק's statement that morning clouds have no substance, based on הושע 6:4.

steps.title: רב פפא: people say morning rain means a full day of rain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי with a popular saying: if it rains when the doors open in the morning, the donkey-driver should just go back to sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But people say, 'When the doors open in the morning and it is raining, donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back. A well-known saying claims that rain in the morning means it will rain all day, so morning clouds seem to be strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If morning rain means a full rainy day, then morning clouds do have substance. That goes against רב יהודה בר יצחק and against אביי's limit.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But people say:
When the doors are opened in the morning and there is rain,
donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep!
phrases.notes: He means there will be no work today, because the rain will last all day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְהָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from step 16 that morning clouds have no substance.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that morning clouds have no substance (steps 15-16).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A common saying treats morning rain as a sign of a full day of rain, so morning clouds seem to be strong.

steps.title: Thick clouds versus light clouds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the saying is about a sky full of thick clouds, while רב יהודה בר יצחק was talking about light clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This saying is about a sky covered with thick clouds. That statement is about a sky covered with light clouds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא by splitting into two kinds of morning skies. Heavy clouds bring a full day of rain, and light clouds bring almost nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements are true, but each one talks about a different case. The popular saying is about thick clouds, and 'morning clouds have no substance' is about light clouds. So אביי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (the two sources talk about different cases)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this saying is about when the sky is covered with thick clouds,
that statement is about when it is covered with light clouds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source talks about a different kind of cloud cover.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Morning rain always means a full day of rain, so morning clouds are strong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thick morning clouds bring a full day of rain. Light morning clouds have no substance, so אביי's limit holds.
steps.whatToRemember: Rain before the evening שמע cancels 'וְעָצַר'. Rain before the morning שמע usually does not, because light morning clouds are weak. Thick morning clouds are a different story.

steps.title: A dry טבת is good for the year
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says a year is blessed when the month of טבת is a 'widow', meaning it has no rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is good for the year when טבת is a widow, meaning it has no rain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב יהודה says that a rainless טבת is good for the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain was called the earth's husband (step 11), so a 'widowed' טבת is a month with no rain. The reason why this is good is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow (here, a month with no rain)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It is good for the year
when Tevet is a widow.
phrases.notes: Rain was called the earth's husband earlier, so a 'widow' month means a month without rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: טָבָא לְשַׁתָּא דְּטֵבֵת אַרְמַלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about rain in טבת. It builds on the 'husband' image from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year in which טבת has no rain is a good year.

steps.title: Two reasons why a dry טבת helps
steps.stepSummary: Two opinions explain רב יהודה: too much rain ruins the gardens, or too much rain causes blight in the crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: so that the gardens are not ruined. And some say: so that the crop does not get blight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two explanations of why a rainless טבת is good. Both say that extra rain in טבת does damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says too much rain ruins vegetable gardens. The second says it causes a crop disease called blight. They agree on the rule and only differ on what kind of damage the rain does.

phrases.english: Some say:
so that the gardens are not ruined,
and some say:
so that the crop does not get blight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב יהודה's statement in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra rain in טבת is harmful, either by ruining gardens or by causing blight.

steps.title: רב חסדא says a muddy טבת is good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with רב חסדא, who says a year is blessed when טבת is muddy from rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב חסדא said: It is good for the year when טבת is muddy and messy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a contradiction. רב חסדא says the exact opposite: a rainy, muddy טבת is good for the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה praises a dry טבת and רב חסדא praises a wet טבת. Both cannot seem to be right about the same month.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Chisda say:
It is good for the year when Tevet is messy!
phrases.notes: 'Messy' here means full of mud from lots of rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's statement from step 19 using an opposite statement by רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that a dry טבת is good (step 19).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא says a rainy, muddy טבת is good, which is the opposite.

steps.title: It depends on whether it rained before טבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה is talking about a year when it already rained before טבת, and רב חסדא about a year when it had not rained yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This is when the rain came at the start of the season. That is when the rain did not come at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by splitting the cases. Whether rain in טבת is good depends on whether the earlier rains already came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it already rained before טבת, more rain in טבת does harm, so a dry טבת is better (רב יהודה). If it had not rained yet, the land needs rain, so a muddy טבת is a blessing (רב חסדא).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is when rain came at the start,
that is when rain did not come at the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דַּאֲתָא מִיטְרָא מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each statement applies to a different kind of year.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה and רב חסדא disagree about whether rain in טבת is good.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dry טבת is good if it already rained before. A rainy טבת is good if it had not rained yet.
steps.whatToRemember: Rain in טבת is not simply good or bad. It depends on whether the land already got rain earlier in the season.

steps.title: Rain on part of a country is not a curse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that if rain falls on part of a country and not on another part, this is not the curse of 'וְעָצַר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Rain that fell on part of a country but not on another part does not count as the curse of 'And He will close up the heavens'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new teaching: rain that falls only in some areas is not the punishment of 'וְעָצַר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse of 'וְעָצַר' means God holds back the rain completely. רב חסדא holds that if some areas still get rain, the curse has not happened.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And He will close up' the heavens, the curse of no rain

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Rain that fell on part of a country
and on part of the country did not fall
does not count as "and He will close up".
phrases.notes: דברים 11:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching of רב חסדא, who was also quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partial rain in a country is not the curse of 'וְעָצַר'.

steps.title: A פסוק in עמוס calls partial rain a curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a פסוק about rain on one city and not another, which רב says is a curse for both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But it says: 'I also held back the rain from you three months before the harvest, and I made it rain on one city and not on another; one field was rained upon...' And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Both are a curse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks on רב חסדא: a פסוק describes rain in one city and not another, and רב says that is a curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said partial rain is not a curse. But רב reads the פסוק as saying that both the rainy place and the dry place are cursed. So partial rain does seem to be a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This opens a challenge
A field, a piece of land

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְגַם אָנֹכִי מָנַעְתִּי מִכֶּם אֶת הַגֶּשֶׁם
phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And I also held back the rain from you
phrases.notes: עמוס 4:7

phrases.english: when there were still three months to the harvest
and I made it rain on one city
and on another city I did not make it rain
one field was rained upon, etc."
And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Both are for a curse!
phrases.notes: He means both the city that got rain and the city that did not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of רב חסדא in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's teaching that partial rain is not a curse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק, as explained by רב, calls rain in one place and not another a curse for both.

steps.title: Too much rain versus the right amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is about too much rain in one place, while רב חסדא is talking about the right amount of rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is when a lot of rain came, and that is when the rain came as much as was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the two sources describe different kinds of rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק and רב are talking about a flood of rain in one place, which ruins it, so both places suffer. רב חסדא is talking about a normal, helpful amount of rain in one area, which is a blessing there and not a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is when a lot of rain came,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the פסוק and רב's 'both are a curse.'

phrases.english: that is when it came as much as was needed.
phrases.notes: 'That' is רב חסדא's case from step 23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: too much rain versus the right amount.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say that any partial rain is a curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only too much rain in one place is a curse. The right amount in one place is not 'וְעָצַר'.

steps.title: The word 'תִּמָּטֵר' shows a flooded place
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports the answer: the word 'תִּמָּטֵר' means the field becomes a 'place of rain', which means a flood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording also shows this, because it says 'תִּמָּטֵר', meaning it will become a place of rain. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support from the words of the פסוק for the answer in step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads 'תִּמָּטֵר' as 'it will be a place of rain', which means flooded with water. So the פסוק itself is talking about too much rain, just like the answer said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact and supports this
A place of rain, a flooded spot
Learn from it; this is proven

steps.whatToRemember: Rain in only part of the land is a curse only when it comes as a flood. The right amount of rain in one area is not 'וְעָצַר'.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The wording is exact too, as it says: "was rained upon"
it will be a place of rain.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 25 from the words of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the curse in the פסוק is too much rain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'תִּמָּטֵר' in עמוס 4:7, read as 'a place of rain'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק is about flooding rain, so רב חסדא's teaching stands.

steps.title: When to start making a ברכה on rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says one makes a ברכה on rain once the 'groom goes out to meet the bride'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: From when does one make a ברכה on rain? From when the groom goes out to meet the bride.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic: רבי אבהו tells us at what point the rain is strong enough to make a ברכה on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is a picture. The raindrops are the 'groom' and the water already on the ground is the 'bride'. Once enough rain has fallen that puddles form and splash up to meet the drops, one makes the ברכה.
steps.confusionAlert: There is no real wedding here. 'Groom' and 'bride' are a picture of falling raindrops meeting the water that is already on the ground.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
From when does one make a blessing on the rain?
From when the groom goes out to meet the bride.
phrases.notes: The drops are the groom and the puddles below are the bride, splashing up to meet them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מֵאֵימָתַי מְבָרְכִין עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the ברכה on rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One makes a ברכה on rain once it has fallen enough that the ground water splashes up to meet the drops.

steps.title: What words does one say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the wording of the ברכה on rain is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What ברכה does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to set up the next step: what are the words of this ברכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו told us when to make the ברכה but not what to say. Now the גמרא asks for the wording.

phrases.english: What blessing does one say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 27 by asking for the text of the ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact words of the ברכה on rain.

steps.title: Thanks for every single drop
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ברכה is: 'We thank You, ה׳ our God, for every drop You brought down for us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: 'We thank You, ה׳ our God, for each and every drop that You brought down for us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the basic wording of the ברכה on rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה is a thank-you. It stresses that each single drop is a gift, not just the rain as a whole.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
"We thank You, ה׳ our God,

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל טִפָּה וְטִפָּה שֶׁהוֹרַדְתָּ לָנוּ״.
phrases.english: for each and every drop that You brought down for us."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה is 'מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ... עַל כׇּל טִפָּה וְטִפָּה שֶׁהוֹרַדְתָּ לָנוּ'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's longer ending for the ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes the ברכה with a long praise, 'If our mouth were full of song like the sea', ending with 'בָּרוּךְ רוֹב הַהוֹדָאוֹת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן ends it like this: 'If our mouth were full of song like the sea, and our tongue full of joyful singing like its many waves...' until 'May Your mercy not leave us, ה׳ our God, and it has not left us. Blessed is the One of many thanks.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds an ending to רב's ברכה, a long praise with a closing ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not argue with רב. He continues the same thank-you and gives it a closing line, 'בָּרוּךְ רוֹב הַהוֹדָאוֹת'. The middle words are left out with 'כּוּ׳' and 'עַד', meaning the full text is known.

keyTerms.meaning: Many thanks; God, who deserves endless thanks

steps.whatToRemember: When enough rain falls, one thanks ה׳ for every drop. רבי יוחנן adds the 'אִילּוּ פִינוּ' praise. The גמרא questions his closing words 'בָּרוּךְ רוֹב הַהוֹדָאוֹת' in step 31, and רבא changes them in step 32.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan concludes it like this:
"If our mouth were full of song like the sea
and our tongue full of joyful singing like its many waves, etc."
until: "May Your mercy not leave us, ה׳ our God,
and it has not left us; blessed is the One of many thanks."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an ending to the wording given in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה continues with 'אִילּוּ פִינוּ' and closes with 'בָּרוּךְ רוֹב הַהוֹדָאוֹת'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's ending adds the 'אִילּוּ פִינוּ' praise. Its closing words are challenged and changed in steps 31-32.

steps.title: Why say 'most of the thanks' and not 'all of the thanks'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ending 'ברוך רוב ההודאות' because it seems to suggest God deserves only most of our thanks, not all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the ברכה say 'most of the thanksgivings' and not 'all of the thanksgivings'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the closing words of רבי יוחנן's ברכה. Saying 'most' thanks seems to give God less than He deserves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ended his ברכה with 'בָּרוּךְ רוֹב הַהוֹדָאוֹת'. The word 'רוב' (most) suggests some thanks are not owed to God. This sounds wrong, because every praise belongs to Him.

keyTerms.meaning: Most, the majority, or a great amount

phrases.english: 'Most of the thanksgivings' and not 'all of the thanksgivings'?
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of רבי יוחנן's ברכה from step 30.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ending wording of the ברכה that רבי יוחנן gave in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The closing words 'ברוך רוב ההודאות' in רבי יוחנן's ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Most' suggests only part of our thanks belongs to God, but all thanks should go to Him.

steps.title: רבא changes the wording to 'God of thanksgivings'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ending should be said as 'אל ההודאות', meaning 'God of thanksgivings'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Say instead 'God of thanksgivings'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the problem by changing the words of the ברכה. Instead of 'רוב ההודאות' we say 'אל ההודאות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not defend the word 'רוב'. He replaces it. 'אל ההודאות' calls God the One to whom thanks belongs, so the problem of 'only most' is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it as; used to change the wording

phrases.english: Rava said: Say instead:
'God of thanksgivings.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברכה ends 'רוב ההודאות', which seems to give God only most of the thanks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה should end 'אל ההודאות', calling God the One to whom thanks belongs.

steps.title: רב פפא begins a practical conclusion
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא opens with 'therefore', starting a practical ruling based on the different versions of the ברכה. His ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רב פפא starts to give a practical ruling, and his words continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הלכך' means 'therefore'. It shows that רב פפא is drawing a practical result from the opinions just quoted. We have not seen his actual ruling yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore; brings in a practical conclusion

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
phrases.notes: His sentence breaks off here. The rest of what he says is on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts drawing a practical result from the different versions of the ברכה in steps 29-32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A practical ruling is coming, based on the different wordings. Its content continues on the next amud.
